evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/meters/MeterReadingScreen.tsx:128-138 — handleSubmit enqueues `addToQueue({ type: 'CREATE', endpoint: '/api/v1/meter-readings', method: 'POST', body: { meterType, reading, unit, photoUri } })`. The endpoint path `/api/v1/meter-readings` DOES NOT EXIST on the api-server. The backend mounts the meters router under `/api/v1/meters` and nests readings at `/readings` (backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/meters.rs:44 `.route("/readings", post(submit_reading))`, documented utoipa path :571 `/api/v1/meters/readings`). A grep of backend/servers/api-server/src for `meter-readings` finds only an S3 key prefix in routes/ai/ocr.rs, never a route. So every POST from this screen hits a non-existent path and returns 404.

Payload shape is also incompatible with the real endpoint. Backend handler submit_reading (meters.rs:579-595) deserializes `Json<SubmitReading>`; SubmitReading (backend/crates/db/src/models/meter.rs:193-204) REQUIRES `meter_id: Uuid` and `reading: Decimal`, with optional `reading_date`, `reading_time`, `source`, `photo_url`. The mobile body sends none of these — it sends a `meterType` string enum (water/electricity/gas/...), `reading` as a raw user string, a `unit` string, and `photoUri`. There is no meter_id anywhere in the mobile flow (the screen selects a hardcoded METER_TYPES enum, not a server meter UUID), so even if the path were corrected the request would 422 on the missing required `meter_id`.

Failure is silent + data-losing. The offline queue classifies the 404 as a TERMINAL 4xx and DROPS the action permanently (frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:437-465, `isPermanent` branch -> droppedPermanent + console.error, action discarded). Meanwhile handleSubmit shows the success/offline Alert OPTIMISTICALLY at enqueue time, before any server round-trip (MeterReadingScreen.tsx:144-152 — t('meters.submitSuccess') / t('meters.savedOffline')). Net effect: NO meter reading submitted from the mobile app can ever persist; the resident is told their reading was saved while it is 404-dropped. This is a complete-feature-breakage + silent-data-loss bug on a core UC (meter self-readings).

Fix (landable in the cloud runner, TS + jest-expo only): point the submit at the real contract — resolve the user's meter UUID for the selected meterType (needs a meter-list/lookup; the screen currently has none) and POST `/api/v1/meters/readings` with `{ meter_id, reading: <numeric>, reading_date?, photo_url? }` per SubmitReading. Add a jest-expo test asserting the queued action's endpoint + body match the OpenAPI/SubmitReading shape (would fail on main today). If the server meter_id is genuinely unavailable on mobile, this is a missing-capability that must be surfaced to the user instead of a fake success.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/meters/MeterReadingScreen.tsx:84-97 captures a photo via ImagePicker and stores the LOCAL device URI in `photoUri` (a `file:///.../ImagePicker/xyz.jpg` path). handleSubmit then puts that raw local URI straight into the JSON submit body: :122 `photoUri: photoUri || undefined` -> :136 `photoUri: readingData.photoUri`. The body is sent as JSON, never multipart: executeQueuedAction serialises it with `JSON.stringify(action.body)` and sends it as a JSON POST (frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:299). No FormData, no presigned-URL upload, no file bytes ever leave the device — only the device-local path string.

The backend field is `photo_url: Option<String>` (backend/crates/db/src/models/meter.rs:203) — a URL to an ALREADY-UPLOADED image, not a client file:// path; note also the name mismatch (`photoUri` vs `photo_url`), so serde would ignore the mobile field even on the correct endpoint. There is no meter-photo upload pipeline on mobile (contrast the sibling fault-photo gap tracked in 2026-09-26, which is a different file/mechanism — faults omit photos entirely; here the photo is 'sent' as an unusable local path). The resident photographs their meter as proof-of-reading, sees success, and the image is silently discarded.

This is a distinct fix from the endpoint bug above: even after the submit is re-pointed to POST /api/v1/meters/readings with a valid meter_id, the photo still needs a real upload (capture -> upload image to storage / presigned URL -> pass the resulting `photo_url` string in SubmitReading), OR the photo picker should be hidden / the user warned that photos are not yet uploaded so no one believes evidence was filed when it was not. Fix is TS-only and cloud-landable; add a jest-expo test asserting a captured photo results in an uploaded URL (not a file:// path) in the submit body.
